title: Forensic Audit Handoff Connector and Indexing Guide
content:
Purpose:
This note defines the handoff connector that moves "control evidence" from our collectors into an indexed forensics store and the SIEM export pipeline. It focuses on message-level guarantees, an evidence-friendly indexing model, RBAC v2 access controls for retrieval, and practical constraints for collectors (edge and sidecar). The doc is intended as an implementation reference and runbook for devs and SREs building or operating the connector.

Background and motivation:
- We currently have multiple collector types (agent sidecar, ingest proxy, batch harvester). Each emits audit-like events with varying shapes.
- Security team needs a deterministic, queryable store for investigation and attestations where each record is immutable, cryptographically verifiable, and can be exported to SIEMs for correlation.
- Existing artifacts focus on ingest and evidence routing; this doc describes the "handoff" layer that: canonicalizes events, attaches provenance metadata, indexes for fast forensic queries, and prepares SIEM exports with minimal transformation.

Goals:
1) Define a compact canonical audit_event schema for handoff that accommodates RBAC v2 context and long-lived evidence attachments.
2) Specify connector-side guarantees: at-least-once delivery to indexing store with de-duplication, tamper-evident checksums, and retention/TTL policy metadata.
3) Provide rules for indexing (primary keys, secondary attributes, tags) tuned for common security queries (actor path, control id, timeline).
4) Map the canonical schema to the SIEM export format and document where enrichment occurs.
5) Enumerate operational playbooks for failures, replays, and legal hold scenarios.

Constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: full redesign of collector protocols — we expect collectors to adapt adapters to the canonical schema.
- Connector should be language-agnostic; implementation can be a stateless streaming service with idempotent sinks.
- Latency SLOs: handoff must not add more than 500ms p50 to the synchronous path for dedicated customers; async collectors may batch.

Canonical audit_event schema (flat-ish key set; compact for storage):
- event_id: string (uuid4)
- occurred_at: string (ISO8601 UTC)
- source: string (collector identifier, e.g., sidecar-az1-12)
- control_id: string (internal control name or id)
- actor: string (user/email/service-account)
- actor_role_path: string (RBAC v2 role path at time of event)
- action: string (allowed values: create/update/delete/grant/revoke/access/execute)
- resource_type: string
- resource_id: string
- payload_digest: string (sha256 hex of canonical payload blob)
- payload_blob_ref: string (object store URI or attachment id)
- provenance: string (signing key id or claim string)
- confidence: string (low/medium/high)
- tags: array[string] (e.g., ["control:auth-login", "sensitivity:high"])
- retention_policy: string (e.g., legal_hold/90d/365d)
- export_flags: string (comma separated to indicate SIEM/CORR/ARCHIVE)

Notes on the payload_blob:
- The blob is the full raw event or evidence artifact (e.g., log fragment, packet capture, config diff). For small events the blob can be inlined; for larger artifacts store externally in the evidence archive and reference via payload_blob_ref.
- The connector calculates payload_digest and verifies a sender-provided digest to detect tampering in transit.

Provenance and tamper-evidence:
- Each connector-run computes an HMAC over (event_id || occurred_at || payload_digest) using a rotation-capable key in KMS. The HMAC is recorded in the provenance field as "hmac:kms-key-2024-09:v1:<hex>".
- For critical control evidence (retention_policy == legal_hold) connectors should attach a signed manifest batch to the archive.

Indexing model and query patterns:
Primary key: event_id (unique)
Secondary indexes (for fast scans):
- actor (exact and prefix)
- control_id
- occurred_at (time range)
- tags (multi-value)
- payload_digest (for dedupe/hit tracking)

Tagging strategy:
- Use colon-delimited tag keys to aid hierarchical search, e.g., "control:payments:3ds" or "team:fraud-detection".
- Include rbv:role and env tags automatically by connector if present in RBAC v2 claim, e.g., "rbac:platform-admin".

Deduplication semantics:
- Connector sink must be idempotent by checking payload_digest + source + occurred_at within a sliding window (configurable, default 24 hours). If duplicates detected, annotate record with "duplicate_of:<event_id>" and keep both records; primary record remains the earliest event_id.
- For replays (bulk re-ingest), a replay_batch_id is required and records must include replay_sequence to preserve ordering. Replayed events must set export_flags=replay.

SIEM export mapping and enrichment:
- SIEM requires flattened events. Connector produces a SIEM-friendly view per event with fields: siem_id(event_id), time, actor, control, severity (derived from tags/confidence), evidence_ref (payload_blob_ref), provenance_hmac.
- Enrichment steps performed by connector (not SIEM): resolve actor to directory id (if available), resolve control_id to canonical control description (from control registry), attach customer/tenant id for multitenant exports.
- Sensitive fields (payload_blob_ref or actor email) should be masked or pseudonymized for exports when export_flags excludes PHI. Masking policy is controlled via per-tenant export profile.

RBAC v2 interactions and access controls:
- Retrieval of evidence from the forensics store is gated by RBAC v2 using attribute-based checks: actor_role_path at event time, requesting_principal, and purpose-of-access tag.
- Connector writes actor_role_path into the event at handoff time. The forensics store enforces access via an entitlement service which interprets RBAC role paths and maps to allowed actions (read/annotate/export).
- Audit trail: every retrieval must generate an access_audit event that is fed back into the evidence pipeline (cross-link via related_event_id).

Operational runbooks (high level):
- Sink write failure: retry with exponential backoff up to N attempts (configurable), then escalate by writing to a cold holding queue (S3 archive) with metadata for later replay.
- Proof mismatch (payload_digest != sender_digest): reject and emit an ingest_error event; quarantine original message into a forensics bucket for manual review.
- Lost attachments: if payload_blob_ref not found in object store, mark event status=orphaned and enqueue attach-notify task to collector team.
- Legal hold: connector must override normal TTL and tag records with retention_policy=legal_hold; these records bypass regular deletion sweeps.

Testing and verification checklist:
- Unit tests for canonicalizer (schema conformance, field normalization).
- Integration tests: collector -> connector -> index -> SIEM export with seeded events including attachments.
- Chaos tests: simulate KMS key rotation, index write latency spikes, and object store unavailability.
- End-to-end RBAC test harness: user with role X attempts read; verify access_audit generated and deny/allow path correct.

Example canonical event (compact JSON example):
{
  "event_id": "8b1a9e2a-3f4d-4c2f-9b22-6a7f7c1d2d9b",
  "occurred_at": "2025-01-10T14:22:31Z",
  "source": "sidecar-usw2-07",
  "control_id": "ctl-auth-err-12",
  "actor": "svc:session-processor@redwood.ai",
  "actor_role_path": "/org/platform/roles/session-processor",
  "action": "access",
  "resource_type": "session",
  "resource_id": "sess_6b3f...",
  "payload_digest": "sha256:2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c...",
  "payload_blob_ref": "s3://evidence-archive/redwood/2025/01/10/8b1a9e2a-blob.gz",
  "provenance": "hmac:kms-key-2024-09:v1:9c3f...",
  "confidence": "high",
  "tags": ["control:auth", "sensitivity:medium"],
  "retention_policy": "365d",
  "export_flags": "SIEM,ARCHIVE"
}

Migration and incremental rollout plan:
- Phase 1: deploy connector in read-only mode for 2 weeks (shadow writes) to validate canonicalization and index load without changing production flows.
- Phase 2: enable write-path for non-critical controls (low sensitivity) and monitor duplicate rates, indexing latency, and storage growth.
- Phase 3: ramp to all controls and enforce retention policies; enable SIEM exports with masking profiles.

Outstanding decisions / open questions:
- Should the connector perform label-based redaction (PII) or defer to downstream pipelines? (tradeoffs: accuracy vs cost/complexity)
- Replay window: default 24h is conservative — legal/forensics team to confirm a recommended policy for cross-tenant investigations.
- HMAC vs signing with customer-provided keys for private deployments: customers running Private may want their own signing keys. Need a design for per-tenant key injection and audit.

Appendix: quick implementation notes for collectors
- Minimal adapter contract: provide event_id, occurred_at, source, payload_blob (or ref), sender_digest. Connector will add actor_role_path if collector can query the RBAC service; otherwise connector will request a role snapshot from identity service.
- Backpressure: collectors should implement backoff and local spool; do not drop legal_hold evidence.

References and links:
- Jira board: https://jira.redwood/projects/EVIDENCE/boards/12
- Control registry (Confluence): confluence://controls/registry
- Evidence collector repo PR for adapter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evidence-collector/pull/487

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus feedback on the schema fields (are we missing critical attributes?), the dedupe semantics, and RBAC v2 integration points.
- If you are implementing a connector, ping #sec-evidence on Slack and tag @Samira for pairing on the HMAC/key rotation design.

End of doc.
